transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. We need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends — this is a decision-bearing review, so we're not deferring approval. The legacy API is scheduled for retirement next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API has hit 98 percent of observed traffic, so it's well past our migration-readiness threshold. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can settle on this, our standard deprecation review requires both the API engineer and customer success to disclose any newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record — a verbal acknowledgement alone won't complete that check. So let's hear from both of you: do you have any newly confirmed evidence to disclose for the record?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to disclose newly confirmed evidence for the formal review record. While investigating an unrelated latency spike, I found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest one needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I only confirmed the traffic identities minutes ago, which is why the deprecation ticket hasn't been updated yet. This is critical because the current draft plan's 7-day notice plus 7-day overlap would not give this integrator enough time to complete their migration safely.
